pages.title: The bucket object contract
pages.purpose: The durable object layout on the bucket: ownership records, node leases, deployment pointer and manifests, wake entries, node log, and the reserved prefixes no application may write.
instructions: Enumerate the concrete key schemes (cells/<cell>/own.json, nodes/<node>.json, deploy/current.json, wake/, etc.) with source citations.
Explain CAS tokens as the conditional-write dialect-neutral mechanism.

pages.title: The decision core (celld-logic)
pages.purpose: How behavioral state advances: Events, Effects, State, the no-IO purity contract, and how the production executor and deterministic simulator feed it.
instructions: Explain on_event as the only state advance and the effect-adapter contract.
Name the major sub-decision modules (pressure, log_tier, wake, queue, isolate) with one line each.

pages.title: Architecture overview
pages.purpose: The node/fleet/cell model, ownership boundaries, the logic-vs-executor layering, and the main data/control flows at a distance.
instructions: Cite the actor/event/effect loop and the two HTTP listeners.
Emphasize the crate ownership split from the workspace comment: logic owns decisions, celld executes effects.

pages.title: Change guide: common maintenance tasks
pages.purpose: Focused walkthroughs for representative changes: adding a Workers API surface, adding an environment variable, touching the ownership/replication protocol, and running the test ladder.
instructions: For each task state where to change (logic core + executor adapter, or config plumbing), and which tests to run, each grounded in source.
Respect the purity boundary: no IO in logic; asyncrt disallow-lint for new execution code.

pages.title: Deployments and generations
pages.purpose: How code changes reach a fleet: deploy build/upload (esbuild), the deploy/current.json pointer, in-place generation adoption, asset serving, and reload.
instructions: Cover reserved classes (cron, D1, KV, queue, workflow) as deploy-time concepts.
Explain generations as the per-process materialization of a deployment.

pages.title: Durability and replication
pages.purpose: The write-acknowledgement path: output gate, LTX capture from WAL, per-cell epoch-prefix uploads, the fleet node-log tier, bundle tiering, and restore.
instructions: Distinguish bucket-proof vs fleet-proof acks and CELLD_DURABILITY modes.
Explain the recoverNodeLog takeover interlock and full-prefix restore rule.

pages.title: Ownership, leases, and fencing
pages.purpose: How exactly-one-owner is earned: conditional acquire, epochs, node lease renewal, self-fencing, and takeover recovery.
instructions: Cover RestoreSpec semantics (fresh/took_over/resume_local) from logic.
Ground the fencing argument in both docs/guarantees.md and the code that implements it.

pages.title: Cell runtime and isolates
pages.purpose: V8 execution: cell lifecycle phases, the runtime manager and stateless worker pool, host services/JS API surface, SQLite storage under the cell, and WebSockets/hibernation.
instructions: Cover the ingress listener including websocket pump and reserve-class routing.
Describe one isolate per cell, synchronous storage ops, and hibernation.

pages.title: Object store integrations
pages.purpose: The three conditional-write dialects (S3/R2, GCS XML, Azure Blob), credential chains, endpoint rules, and the startup storage probe.
instructions: Ground that GCS uses generation preconditions, not If-Match; Azure uses If- headers on Put Blob.
List the qualified and disqualified stores per docs/guarantees.md.

pages.title: Peer network and fleet authentication
pages.purpose: The internal listener: signed peer HMAC protocol, tunnels, probes, node-log routes, the /do/ and /runtime/ operator routes, and operator CLIs reaching reserved cells.
instructions: Cite the HMAC headers, replay window, and fleet/peer-auth.json bootstrap.
Explain why operator CLIs forward through a live node instead of writing the bucket.

pages.title: CLI and operator surface
pages.purpose: The celld command tree: daemon flags, deploy, dev, cell list, d1, kv, queue, diagnose, health and /state routes, and JSON output contracts.
instructions: Ground each subcommand in its module; note dev mode's local store and watch loop.

pages.title: Configuration, limits, and memory pressure
pages.purpose: Environment-variable configuration, isolate pool limits, memory-pressure classification and shedding, and operational knobs for replication and compaction.
instructions: Cover concurrency limits (CELLD_MAX_CELL_REQUESTS, activations) and the 503 overload behavior.
Distinguish the pressure threshold, absolute cap, and V8 heap limit; cite the cgroup working-set math.

pages.title: Telemetry and observability
pages.purpose: Traces and logs: the Parquet bucket sink, OTLP sink, retention, sampling, and what events are recorded.
instructions: Cover both sinks, defaults, and the v0-unstable schema caveat from docs/telemetry.md.

pages.title: Testing strategy
pages.purpose: The four layers: differential conformance against workerd, TLA+ model checking, deterministic simulation of the decision core, and live fleet fault injection; plus lint/typecheck discipline.
instructions: Cite the conformance_world_* gates and celld_internal_tests cfg machinery in lib.rs.
Explain the release Dockerfile test/clippy stage; add a short how-to build-and-check section grounded in the Dockerfile and Cargo workspace.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Build, run, and operate celld for the first time: dev mode, deploy, a small fleet, and the diagnosis loop.
instructions: Practical and command-first; every command must be grounded in README.md, docs/, or the CLI source.
State the prerequisite facts (esbuild, supervisor restart, bucket conditional writes) with citations.
